teaser.text: FedEx sells a promise: it will move a package through an air-and-ground network and deliver it by a chosen time or day. A dollar comes in from the shipper and goes out through the people, vehicles, aircraft, facilities, and outside carriers needed to keep that promise.

stock.opening: FedEx's weighted price reaches $334.17 in October 2029, after $225.52 in October 2027; bear, base and bull probabilities are 28%, 52%, and 20%. The investment turns on whether FedEx can convert Network 2.0 savings into durable margin while keeping service reliable.
stock.closing: The full FedEx memo also explains its business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could FedEx's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $225.52 in October 2027, a 21% loss including dividends. It is $269.64 in October 2028, a 5% loss. By October 2029, it reaches $334.17, a 19% gain.
The bear receives 28% probability, while the base receives 52%. The bull receives 20%, reflecting greater execution demands.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for FedEx, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit rises in the base case because volume, pricing and network savings improve gradually. It starts at $6,200M in October 2027 and reaches $6,800M in October 2028, then $7,400M in October 2029. The base revenue path moves from $98B to $102B and then $106B. Margins move from 6.3% through 6.7% to 7.0%, still below management’s 8% target.

The bear case uses $5,200M first, then $5,000M, before recovering to $5,400M. It assumes revenue of $98B at a 5.3% margin initially, followed by weak service and transition costs. The bull case rises from $6,800M to $7,700M and then $8,500M, as revenue reaches $112B and profitable density exceeds the base case. Wages and purchased transportation rose 8% and 9%, so execution remains the central risk.

blocks.heading: How much cash does FedEx really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash left after capital spending. FedEx collects shipping payments, pays employees, fuel suppliers, and contractors, then buys aircraft or sorting equipment; what remains after those payments can support debt repayment, dividends, or buybacks. Because aircraft and facilities are bought at uneven times, one year’s free cash flow is not a permanent earning rate.

The bear case holds at $4.88 because the board reviews the payment annually and the post-spin company still faces labor, capex and transition demands.

blocks.heading: Does FedEx's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: In FY26, operating activities provided $8.925 billion. Capital expenditures were $3.809 billion. The rough remainder was $5.116 billion before other investing and financing decisions. This is not FedEx’s official free-cash-flow measure, but it shows why the company could invest and still return money to owners.

Free cash flow is operating cash left after capital spending. FedEx collects shipping payments, pays employees, fuel suppliers, and contractors, then buys aircraft or sorting equipment; what remains after those payments can support debt repayment, dividends, or buybacks. Because aircraft and facilities are bought at uneven times, one year’s free cash flow is not a permanent earning rate.

earnings.opening: FedEx's next results are expected on October 28, 2026. FedEx must show that Network 2.0 savings are becoming durable margin while service remains reliable.
earnings.closing: The full FedEx memo answers what its business is, how it compares with rivals, who manages it, and what risks could disrupt the plan.

blocks.heading: What has FedEx guided for calendar 2026?

paragraphs.text: The weighted path is weak at first and positive by the final date, hinging on recurring network savings, reliable service, and stronger margins. Calendar 2026 guidance calls for 11% revenue growth and diluted EPS of $16.55–$17.75. Adjusted diluted EPS is $16.90–$18.10. The 2029 framework targets about $98 billion of revenue and $8 billion of operating income. It targets an 8% operating margin. FedEx targets about $2 billion of cumulative Network 2.0 and One FedEx savings by the end of 2027.

Management’s calendar-year forecast uses recast 2025 continuing operations, which excludes FedEx Freight after its spin-off. It also gave a separate estimate for the transition period and said most of that period’s adjusted operating income would arrive in the final quarter, following the company’s usual peak-season pattern.

blocks.heading: Has FedEx kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Raj Subramaniam has led FedEx as CEO since 2022, after joining the company in 1991 and becoming chief operating officer in 2019. His main project is DRIVE, a cost and operating transformation introduced in December 2022. FedEx says it exceeded its $1 billion transformation-savings target for fiscal 2026, but lasting savings matter more than a single milestone.

blocks.heading: What should FedEx watch for in its next results?

paragraphs.text: The call covers June through September, so management should explain how those results fit the seven-month transition estimate and the full calendar-year outlook. The important evidence will not be EPS alone. Operating cash flow, capex and service performance will show whether the plan is producing the intended operating improvement.

paragraphs.subsection: 7.6 — Whether transformation savings reach operating profit
paragraphs.text: UPS reported an adjusted operating margin of 9.8% for full-year 2025, offering useful context for the efficiency gap. FedEx must now show that its savings remain after implementation costs and labor pressure. Management promises a denser network and lower costs; analysts offer a limited earnings yardstick; the decisive proof will be recurring cash and improving margins.
